To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the frequency of mental disorders in the population is very high and that the need for treatment is very great.
the prevalence of psychic diseases in the population is 18.5%; that the frequency of neuroses in the Munich population is 12.8%; and that the frequency of psychosomatic diseases is 5.7%.
the frequency of mental diseases is very high, the majority of the patients can be treated in general practice and the need for specialist care is relatively small.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of the relationship of the psychiatric patient to the general practitioner and the psychiatrist and the question of how this relationship could best be organized.
the question of the extent to which the population is affected by psychiatric diseases and how the existing facilities for treatment and care should be adjusted to the actual need.
a more detailed description of mental disorders in the population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
psychiatric epidemiology has not yet reached the stage at which the results of investigations can be directly used for the planning of psychiatric care.
psychiatric disorders are not only a problem of the hospital and the psychiatrist but rather of the whole community and the whole of medicine.
the need for psychiatric treatment is considerably underestimated and that the practising physician has to be given more opportunity to deal with the psychiatric patient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the frequency of psychiatric diseases is considerably higher than previously assumed.
the frequency of mental disorders is much higher than is generally thought.
the frequency of mental diseases in the general population and the need for treatment are considerably higher than has been hitherto assumed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the practising physician has a great responsibility in this area.

the psychiatric hospital should not be regarded as the only place where psychiatric patients should be treated but rather that the psychiatric hospital is a place where patients can be treated who are not being treated in the community.
the practising physician should be trained in psychiatric diagnosis, therapy and prophylaxis.
